audit_question.question: When F3 is established by a matching prepare-reply threshold, can a legal later attempt replace previously accepted commands with client-proposal commands or NOOP despite preparation reporting those commands, or do the reply producer, attempt initialization, quorum configuration, or committed-instance handling exclude the consequential history?
audit_question.importance: The threshold-selected commands are passed directly into outgoing Accept messages. If a legal later attempt can replace an already decided value and obtain sufficient acceptance, replicas could apply different operations for one instance. The current source establishes replacement and propagation, but not that consequential execution.
contexts: An instance with possible prior accepted commands
A later preparation attempt reaching the local reply threshold
event_paths: Earlier acceptance -> later preparation -> matching reply records commands by VBallot -> threshold overwrites lb.cmds -> bcastAccept sends overwritten commands
counterevidence: handlePrepareReply rejects replies below lastTriedBallot and routes higher-ballot replies through a nack branch; the observed overwrite requires matching ballots.
handlePropose increments crtInstance before initializing a proposal instance, so ordinary fresh proposal admission alone does not establish reuse of an earlier accepted instance.
handlePropose can bypass preparation when lastTriedBallot equals smallestDefaultBallot; the selected suspicion concerns the preparation threshold path.
F3 describes a local assignment, not a quorum-backed selected-value guarantee. An applicable requirement still needs the producer and legal-history analysis.
Committed-instance response and mutation protections remain navigation-based possibilities until their exact source is attached.
unknowns: Whether PrepareReply.Command and VBallot represent prior acceptance in the relevant legal history, including empty commands and initialization sentinels.

audit_question.trigger_rationale: The attached handler first records commands from a greater VBallot, then unconditionally replaces lb.cmds with client commands or NOOP at the threshold. The attached bcastAccept reads that same lb.cmds without further value selection. This resolves the immediate overwrite and downstream-use discriminator; producer semantics and legal prior-acceptance histories remain decisive.
